title: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity
claim: Learning a generative prior from indirect observations works by alternating guided posterior sampling with persistent latent updates and flow-matching training on those latents.
layout: 2 stacked panels (E-step, M-step), left-to-right flow, red dashed gradient-update loops
description: A two-part flow diagram split by a dashed horizontal line. The top part, labeled 'E step: Guided sampling and latent update', starts at a green protein structure (harmonic prior x0). It goes into a blue Flow Model box, which outputs a denoised structure x̂1. That structure goes into an orange Forward Renderer box, which produces a rendered image ŷ. A pink L_rend box compares this to the raw observed image y. Red dashed arrows carry gradient updates back to x_t and to the grey persistent latent x̃. A guided sample ~ p(x|y) is tied to the latent through an L_latent box. The bottom part, 'M Step: Flow matching training using latents', interpolates between the prior x0 and the latent x̃, feeds the result to the Flow Model, and applies an L_flow loss. A red dashed arrow labeled 'update θ' goes back to the model. Black arrows show the main data flow, and red marks the updates.
caption: Overview of EB-FM, illustrated for the cryo-EM setting. Each observation yi is associated with a persistent latent ˜xi that tracks the posterior mean. In the E-step, the current flow matching prior pθ(x) generates a posterior sample ˆxi via gradient-based guidance through the differentiable forward operator A, and ˜xi is updated by EMA. In the M-step, the prior is trained by conditional flow matching on the persistent latents {˜xi} in place of clean data.
abstract: We address the problem of learning generative priors over high-dimensional latent variables from indirect, noisy observations, with a focus on continuous heterogeneity in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). In this setting, 3D atomic structures $x \in \mathbb{R}^{3N_a}$ are never directly observed and must be inferred from 2D projection images $y$ generated by a complex, non-linear forward operator. We propose Empirical Bayes Flow Matching (EB-FM), a method that learns a flow matching prior $p_Î¸(x)$ directly from observations using a Monte Carlo stochastic approximation Expectation-Maximization framework. EB-FM alternates between an E-step that performs approximate posterior sampling from $p_Î¸(x \mid y)$ via guided flow-based generation while maintaining persistent latent estimates through stochastic approximation, and an M-step that updates the flow model using these stabilized latent variables as training targets. This approach eliminates the need for pretraining on clean data and naturally accommodates non-linear forward models. We validate our method on controlled inverse problems using two-moons and MNIST data, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated cryo-EM data with known poses, showing that EB-FM can recover continuous distributions of protein conformations directly in atomic-coordinate space.
